AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation Measures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation Measures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation Measures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation Measures.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning the Kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning the Kitchen.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning the Kitchen.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning the Kitchen.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen.

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Cleaning the Kitchen and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Sewing Skills: Constructing Household Items 14 4.2 Constructing Innovative Anima and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Sewing Skills: Constructing Household Items and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Constructing Innovative Animal Waterer 10 4.3 ICT Support Services 9 Total Numbe and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

2. A — Ice melting to water

3. B — 100 °C

4. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen.

10. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
